openings.claim: Switching may delay picking/checking independently of complexity.
openings.discriminator: Same-layout switch penalty versus compartment-count effect.
openings.probe: Both workers counterbalance repeats/interleaving; fix color; time stages/errors using reusable samples.

openings.claim: Order-specific short-partition diagrams may improve arrangement.
openings.discriminator: Fewer placement errors/help requests with complete kits.
openings.probe: Ten participants compare diagrams on matched layouts; verify contents; measure completion and preparation costs/time.

openings.claim: Ship loose partitions with inventory/layout sheets; customers perform insertion.
openings.discriminator: Preparation/checking saves insertion time; nine of ten arrange unaided.
openings.probe: Ten sets versus assembled samples: time stages/sheets; check arrangement, completeness, capacity, damage.
openings.uncertainty: Mapping, distinguishability, customer ability, packaging retention required.

openings.claim: Replace shared-bin picking with prepared trays and verified worker handoff.
openings.probe: Five reusable samples; matched mixed sequences, alternate roles, rare colors; measure worker-minutes, elapsed time, errors, setup/waiting.
openings.uncertainty: Space, lists/color identification, replenishment, checking required; insertion difficulty persists.

decision: Probe, then decide. All require 30x20 cm, same assortment, removable partitions, initial <=500, added materials <=0.40/order, accepted counts/colors and fixed delivery. Reuse <=15 samples. Reports do not verify omissions; width overlap leaves insertion cause unresolved. Small probes cannot establish pilot targets: >=98% complete, median <=8 minutes, >=90% unaided.
